newsitem.title: UK: U.S.'s Daley hopes for progress between EU/Boeing.
newsitem.headline: U.S.'s Daley hopes for progress between EU/Boeing.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Secretary William Daley said on Wednesday that he was hopeful that progress could be made between the European Commission and U.S. aircraft giant Boeing Co over its proposed merger with McDonnell Douglas.
The European Union has threatened to block a proposed merger between Boeing and McDonnell Douglas
"We are optimistic that progress will be made between the parties," Daley told reporters.

"We obviously believe this merger is good for the companies, good for competitiveness and good for customers around the world." He said he did not think the Commission was saying the merger could not take place. "What they are saying is that there are ramifications if it goes ahead and they will act on those."
But he would not say whether the U.S. administrations thought a Commission move to block the merger would have any legal force.

The EU is to announce its final decision on the merger on July 23. EU officials said last week that the merger plan in its current state was "not sufficient" under EU antitrust law and threatened to block it if changes were not made.
